purpose: Start with territorial control, then trace distinct economic beneficiaries

sources.title: Colonies and dependencies from 1782 — statistical blue books
sources.evidence: Colonial governments annually returned staff/military figures, local taxes and revenue, spending, budgets, trade and shipping
sources.risk: Non-standardised columns and missing years; cannot infer metropolitan profit from gross local revenue

sources.title: Colonial Office: Queensland Miscellanea / blue books
sources.evidence: CO 238 series of Queensland statistical blue books 1859–1920, 62 volumes
sources.risk: Series metadata not individual audited fiscal facts; Australian regional source not automatically global

sources.title: 1833 Slavery Abolition and Compensation Claims
sources.evidence: T 71 slave registrations and claims; NDO 4 compensation payments
sources.risk: Compensation to slaveowners; not abolition compensation paid to the enslaved; payments cannot be added to shipping profit

sources.title: Legacies of British Slave-Ownership
sources.evidence: 1833 slaveholder/plantation/compensation network, tracks estate ownership back to 1763; UCL states >40,000 slaveowners at 1833 abolition
sources.risk: Ownership ≠ investor ≠ shipment; owner can have multiple properties; rights to copy database unverified

sources.title: Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database downloads
sources.evidence: December 2019 download with 36,108 voyages total across national participation; 274 variables
sources.risk: ALL nationalities, not British voyage count; individual rows incomplete; method uses imputation, deduplicate by voyage ID and data version

sources.title: Methodology: Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database
sources.evidence: How observed vs imputed values, ports and captive counts are constructed; voyages not all equal one voyage of British origin
sources.risk: Database completeness uneven by region/time and some location values imputed; cannot treat all as exact point lines

sources.title: India Office Economic Department Records
sources.evidence: Revenue and economic departments; relevant to India fiscal system and opium/salt/customs
sources.risk: The catalogue is not a profit ledger; institution and dates of series span long time; company and crown government distinct

sources.title: Colonial Revenue and Expenditure — 25 Feb 1823
sources.evidence: Debate contrasting local colonial revenues and British military/civil expenditures, with individual-year examples
sources.risk: Speaker's reported numbers in parliamentary debate, not independently audited; colonial revenues not London treasury transfer

sources.title: Revenues of the Crown — 28 April 1820
sources.evidence: Returns on Crown receipts, West Indies duties and some Gibraltar surplus remittances 1760–1820
sources.risk: Different accounting windows and categories; material often earmarked for salaries/other disbursements; do not compare without controls

sources.title: Supply — 10 May 1830
sources.evidence: Contemporaneous Treasury communications on deficits of selected crown colonies over prior multi-year period
sources.risk: Debate/quoted correspondence rather than independently checked accounts; selection excludes many colonies

sources.title: West India Planters Petition, 12 March 1807
sources.evidence: Planters' explicit contemporaneous economic argument distributing sugar price among duties, freight, commissions and others
sources.risk: Interested-party lobbying, not empirical audit; useful for actors/category structure only

illustrative_claims_pending_original_acc.display_use: illustrates need to retain expense and local revenue separately; do not interpret as British profit or loss

illustrative_claims_pending_original_acc.raw_statement: Reported surplus of Gibraltar revenue remitted to England from 1760 to 1820 after garrison expenses: £124,256 10s 7d
illustrative_claims_pending_original_acc.display_use: illustrates remittance differs from local revenue and total imperial gain; caveat broad interval
